flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.reason: Opt-in band: Law 20/2017 requires express written, revocable consent to use identifiable record data and samples for research (Arts. 48, 50, 51), mandatory Research Ethics Committee approval (Art. 48.6) and sanctions (Arts. 54-61). Kept near the bottom because no public transparency register was verified.
flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.published_summary: Identifiable record data cannot be used for research without express written consent, and an ethics committee must approve research on people. Use with identities removed needs no consent and has no opt-out.

flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.reason: An EFDA software-as-medical-device guideline (GDL-094, 2026) exists, but its text was unreadable, so AI/ML coverage, binding force and change control are not verified. A June 2026 news story shows AI diagnostics being deployed with no governance mentioned. Bottom of the guidance-only band.
flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.published_summary: The Ethiopian Food and Drug Authority's AI medical device guideline took effect in June 2026, with change control and rollback rules for learning models. Same regime as Rwanda, but scored in the lower half because most of the text says should, not shall.

flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.reason: The national patient record (DPI) connects 258 facilities in 13 regions (405 per the government page) with 7.3M patients, and clinicians see prior history at other connected hospitals. It is limited to public hospitals, with no verified consent or emergency rules: Mixed band.
flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.published_summary: In facilities on the shared record, a clinician can open a patient's earlier visits and treatments from another equipped site. That covers public facilities in the network only, and private providers are not yet linked.

flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.reason: No verified patient access right (both gazette PDFs unreadable, app page truncated), so band 15-35. A unified national electronic file reachable from any facility was announced for rollout from summer 2026, but it is clinician-facing and not yet delivered, so the score stays in the lower part of the band.
flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.published_summary: Law 18-07 gives a right to a copy of one's data, requested provider by provider, and the controller may ask the regulator for longer reply times. The ministry's citizen app to view the record and test results is announced, not live.

flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.reason: Only the title of Law n°1/03 of 10 March 2026 could be verified. The law PDF is a scanned image and the X post and health policy could not be read, so an access right and a portal are not verified. That gives the 15-35 band, lower half under the evidence rule.
flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.published_summary: Since March 2026, Law 1/03 gives a free copy of your data within one month, but medical information goes only through a doctor you name. No national patient portal was found, and the data regulator does not exist yet, so the score sits at 40.

flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.reason: No enforceable right verified (law PDF unreadable), so 15-35 band, lower half by the evidence rule; one hospital gives on-site viewing or a paper copy on written request; the national electronic record (Apr 2026) has no patient access.
flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.published_summary: Articles 38, 39 and 41 of Law 007/PR/2015 give a right to see and copy your health data, directly or through a health professional. A copy can be charged at reproduction cost, a reply is due within one month, and there is no national portal.

flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.reason: Minister's Order 01-1/n (2019) made the national EHR mandatory for inpatient and outpatient facilities by 1 Jan 2020. Doctors see all visible episodes, patients control visibility, and emergency access is logged. Controlled-drug e-prescriptions are central (2022 order). That is the Strong band, mid, because real-world usage figures are not verified.
flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.published_summary: An authorised doctor who enters a patient's ID number and birth date can see every episode the patient has not hidden, from any facility. The state auditor says family and rural doctors have no access and 24% of active doctors are not connected.

flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.reason: Statutory access right not verified (Act and Regulations PDFs unreadable), so band 15-35 under the evidence rule. Hospital record systems reach 92% of targeted hospitals, but patient self-service portals are only planned, so the score sits mid-band.
flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.published_summary: The 2019 Act lets a patient confirm what a provider holds, get a description and learn who received it, within 30 days and with no listed fee. The right to a full copy rests on a 2009 Ministry charter, and there is no national portal.

flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.reason: Statutory-right formula: base 45, +5 because Ley 7593/25 Art. 28 gives free access with a 30-day deadline, -5 because the law takes effect only 24 months after publication, +5 for the official IPS 'MI IPS' portal showing consultations and dispensed medicines. The electronic clinical record bill was rejected and archived in May 2026.
flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.published_summary: No law in force was found that gives patients a copy of their full clinical record; the constitution's habeas data covers official and public-character registers only. Ley 7593 adds a free access and copy right, but not until November 2027.

flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.reason: The access right in Loi 2022-59 could not be verified (PDF unreachable), and the data protection authority HAPDP was abolished by decree on 8 June 2026 with its duties moved to ministries. No portal found: band 15-35, lower part.
flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.published_summary: Article 69 of Law 2022-59 gives a right to see your data on site or get a copy, but the copy can be charged at reproduction cost and no deadline is set. There is no national patient portal.

flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.reason: The university blog says the record legally belongs to the patient but no specific rule lets patients get copies, and there is no national electronic record or portal. That is the no-enforceable-right band (15-35), mid-low because the Norma Técnica, Ley 3131 and the Constitution could not be read.
flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.published_summary: A 2008 Health Ministry norm says patients may not be refused access to their record and may get a certified paper or digital copy, but it sets no deadline and asks patients not in hospital for a notarised request. No national patient portal exists.

flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.reason: 20-35 band: the only verified fact is that DoctorSV (launched Nov 2025) gets bundled consent through its terms at registration to use anonymised data for research. No opt-out or patient-visible access log was verified, because neither the decree nor the clinical record standard could be read.
flagged_for_editors_abs_diff_ge_15.published_summary: Health data may be used for care without consent, and each person's digital record is open to all public providers, with no opt-out. Every access must be logged and the data law lets patients learn who consulted their data, but practice was not verified.
